items.title: Tyson Foods closing beef plants amid U.S. cattle shortage
items.summary: The meatpacker will shut its Joslin, Illinois, and Eagle Mountain, Utah, facilities and pursue the sale of its Pasco, Washington, plant

items.title: Tyson Foods consolidates beef plants
items.summary: Tyson Foods has based its decision around what it said is "one of the most historic cattle shortages the country has ever experienced".

items.title: China’s Booming Auto Exports Test Shipping Industry
items.summary: China’s auto factories are building so many cars for export that the global shipping industry can’t keep up, the WSJ Logistics Report’s Paul Berger writes.  Specialized car carriers are booked out years ahead to export cars from Chinese factories.  Rates to charter the roll-on/roll-off, or ro-ro, ships are up 65% this year on the surging demand.

items.title: Tyson Foods will close or sell three US beef facilities as industry struggles
Tyson Foods to Exit More Beef Plants, With Cattle in Short Supply
items.summary: U.S. meatpacking companies have been squeezed by a shortage of cattle with domestic supplies falling to their lowest level in 75 years.

items.title: Tyson to Close More Beef Plants as US Cattle Shortage Drags On
items.summary: Tyson Foods Inc. said it would close several additional beef plants, in the latest sign of the US beefpacking industry’s restructuring amid a prolonged US cattle shortage.

items.title: Tyson to Exit More Beef Plants
items.summary: Tyson Foods said it was closing its Joslin, Ill., plant, which employs more than 2,000 people and can kill about 3,000 cattle a day, according to an internal company memo. The Arkansas-based company separately aims to sell its Pasco, Wash.

items.title: The Top 5 Analyst Questions From Tyson Foods’s Q2 Earnings Call
items.summary: Tyson Foods’ second quarter results were shaped by solid execution in its branded Prepared Foods and Chicken segments, even as overall sales were flat year on year and missed Wall Street’s revenue expectations. Management emphasized that consumer demand for protein remained steady, with Prepared Foods gaining both volume and dollar market share due to effective marketing and product innovation.
